device_power_states.description: Radio + MCU in deep sleep; lowest current; the dominant state for a Class A device.
Transmitting a LoRa frame; highest instantaneous current (TX power).
Receiver active during RX1/RX2 (Class A), ping slots (Class B), or continuously (Class C).

class_power_summary.A: Lowest average power; radio off except for TX + two short RX windows; battery life years.
class_power_summary.B: Medium; periodic beacon + ping slots add scheduled RX wakeups.

low_power_modes_summary.sleep: Deep sleep between transmissions dominates the energy budget; CSS time-on-air and TX power set the active energy.
low_power_modes_summary.adr_savings: ADR lowers SF and TX power for good links, cutting time-on-air and energy.

fields.notes: LoRa is built for multi-year battery life: a Class A device sleeps almost always and wakes only to transmit and briefly receive. Spreading factor and TX power dominate active energy (higher SF = longer time-on-air = more energy), which is why ADR is central to the power model.

extraction_hints: Look for power-domain partitioning, supply nets.
